fragmentExecutionLogs.text: Worked on the backend for a couple of hours today. Rahul helped me figure out why the API wasn't responding properly. Still feels like there's a lot I don't understand.
Had a pretty unproductive morning. Kept switching between the backend and random YouTube videos. Need to get more disciplined about this.
Talked to R about the authentication issue. He thinks the middleware is probably where I'm messing something up. Going to look at that tomorrow.
Finally understood a bit of the auth flow today. The middleware thing makes much more sense now. Still need to clean up the API though.
Spent most of today working on the Cognitive Engine. The basic capture part is actually working surprisingly well. Need to figure out what comes after memory.
Rahul asked how the Cognitive Engine is coming along. Told him the memory search works but the actual intelligence part is still pretty basic.
Didn't really work today. Was supposed to work on the engine but ended up going out with friends in the evening. Feeling a little guilty about wasting the day.
Started reading about knowledge graphs. At first it sounded unnecessarily complicated, but I think it might actually make sense for the project.
R sent me a paper about entity resolution. Haven't read it properly yet but the idea of connecting different names to the same thing seems important.
Worked on entity extraction today. The annoying part is that the model sometimes identifies things that aren't actually entities. Need some kind of strict filter.
Had another discussion with Rahul about the project. We went through the backend architecture and he pointed out that I was trying to build too much at once.
I think he's right. I should probably finish one complete pipeline instead of constantly adding new features.
Spent the afternoon fixing the API routes. Nothing major, just a bunch of stupid little issues that somehow took forever.
The backend is finally feeling less messy. Still not happy with the way some of the database stuff is organized though.
Started working on the knowledge graph properly today. Entities, aliases, relationships, provenance... there's a lot going on.
Got confused between the project name and the actual topic today. Need to be careful about how these things are classified.
Rahul mentioned that the resolver shouldn't confidently match two things just because their names look similar. That probably explains some of the weird results I was seeing.
Tried the resolver again with a few variations of the same name. Much better this time. The alias thing seems pretty useful.
Worked on the API again. I keep saying I'm going to stop touching it and move on, and then I find one more thing that needs fixing.
Had a decent day today. Got the capture to memory to graph flow working end to end. It's not perfect, but at least there's finally a proper pipeline.
Didn't mention Rahul by name today but spoke to him about the backend. He suggested keeping the first version simple and testing it with real journal entries.
I'm going to do that. Instead of inventing more test cases, I want to see what happens when the system processes actual messy writing.
Tested a few entries and noticed that some things are getting created twice. Need to check whether the resolver is failing or whether extraction itself is the problem.
The duplicate problem seems to happen mostly when I describe the same thing differently. This is probably exactly what the alias system is supposed to help with.
Took a break from coding and went for a walk. Came back with a much clearer idea of how the graph should work. Sometimes stepping away actually helps.
Worked on the entity resolver again. I don't want it making aggressive guesses. If it's genuinely unsure, I'd rather have it say ambiguous than silently create the wrong connection.
The graph is starting to look useful. I can see the project, the people involved, the technical topics, and some of the things I've been working on repeatedly.
One thing I'm still worried about is all these mentioned-with relationships. Just because two things appear in the same journal entry doesn't necessarily mean they're actually related.
I think the next real challenge is figuring out what the system can actually conclude from the graph without making things up. That's probably where the reasoning part comes in.
Looking back over the last few days, I've spent a ridiculous amount of time on backend and API problems. At least the system now has enough information to potentially notice patterns like that.
